findings.claim: The Goal 1 inventory is declared to exist, but the repoint/removal footprint it hands to the plan is measured by port number (13 files with 7892) rather than by the daemon's identity, so a plan built from it will leave most of the sovereign-sync surface untouched.
findings.evidence: grep -rl 'sovereign-sync|sovereign_sync' over scripts, shared, skills/learn, skills/process, tools/prometheus-cli/crates, hooks, manifests = 33 files, plus 41 under docs/ and site/docs. Absent from the artifact: scripts/install-binaries.sh, scripts/install-system.js, scripts/docs-sync.mjs, scripts/install-sovereign-sync-sharing.sh, scripts/certify-prometheus-exec-use-cases.py, prometheus-cli commands/{doctor,setup}.rs, src/main.rs, tests/{doctor,kbd_device_authority}.rs. sovereign-client/src/client.rs has 7892 only in a doc comment and #[cfg(test)].
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 7892 footprint with a name-based footprint tagged install-script / CLI / probe / doc / test, and drop client.rs from active clients.

findings.claim: The two-node evidence baseline names a single-process byte-compatibility test as an anchor and attributes it to the wrong crate.
findings.evidence: domain_sync.rs has 4 #[tokio::test] + 1 #[test]; the #[test] at line 44 is mobile_wire_is_byte_compatible_with_sovereign_sync, which opens one Runtime in a tempdir with no iroh endpoint. It is not in substrate/kbd-mobile.
findings.suggested_fix: State 4 two-node async tests + 1 single-process wire-compat test; name only the async tests as two-node anchors.

findings.claim: Gap 6 reframes a surface Goal 2 explicitly mandates (REST/MCP/SSE) as an open decision, inviting analyze to drop a stated goal instead of resolving a goal-versus-spec conflict.
findings.evidence: Goals: 'provides the KBD control plane (runtime authority, signed commands, REST/MCP/SSE)'. Companion spec §15 and HMA's desktop prescription conflict with that surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite gap 6 as a goal/spec conflict; the open question is only whether the Companion UI additionally consumes via Tauri IPC and which spec section must be amended.

findings.claim: Goal 3's device identity and pairing is rolled up as existing in sovereign-sync, but the Companion spec describes a different pairing protocol and falsely attributes Noise to sovereign-sync; the conflict is not recorded as a gap.
findings.evidence: grep -il noise over sovereign-sync src and Cargo.toml returns nothing; Companion spec L66, L122, L222 say 'sovereign-sync (Noise + Iroh)'. sovereign-sync pairing is ticket + group_secret + endpoint allowlist over iroh TLS.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a gap: analyze must choose one pairing design and the spec's Noise attribution must be corrected.

findings.claim: The artifact says the Companion's open phase is unassessed with an untouched progress.json while quoting that phase's assess handoff; real state is assessed on disk, transition never recorded.

findings.suggested_fix: State the on-disk versus runtime discrepancy and carry it into the Q3 handoff design.

findings.evidence: ideation-and-decision-tools, kimi-desktop-extensibility, mobile-skill-portability, prometheus-exec-code-execution-engine, uar-host-execution, openspec-mirror-drift-cleanup all lack top-level generatedBy; kbd-runtime lib.rs:5210-5211 'This loop runs over every phase on every transition'.

findings.claim: The unwrap() ban is narrowed to src-tauri/src/, which is the enforcement grep's scope, not the rule's.

findings.claim: The C-01 note conflates repo .mcp.json with the user-level ~/.claude/mcp-servers.json that --sharing actually writes.
